extracted.intended_audience: patent owners, patent practitioners (patent attorneys), and parties adverse to patent owners
extracted.subtask_description: Summarizes USPTO final rules implementing AIA supplemental examination (35 U.S.C. §257) and related ex parte reexamination fee changes, including procedural requirements, limits, fees, content requirements, and strategic recommendations for patent owners and adverse parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of information eligible for supplemental examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplemental examination permits a patent owner to request that information be "considered, reconsidered, or corrected" before the USPTO; such information is not limited to patents or printed publications or even prior art information but may include any information the patent owner believes to be relevant to the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All information must be submitted in written form (non-written information like audio/video must be converted to written transcripts). Relevant documents include patent and non-patent publications, written communications, affidavits, declarations, and transcripts.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO must decide SNQ within three months and issue certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: In response to a supplemental examination request, the USPTO must determine, within three months, whether a substantial new question of patentability (SNQ) affecting any claim is raised by the information and then issue a supplemental examination certificate stating the result.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The supplemental examination commences with receipt of the request and concludes with issuance of the certificate; timing is therefore critical to obtain statutory protections before unenforceability is asserted in litigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim-limited SNQ review (generally)
rubrics_metrics.description: By rule the USPTO will generally limit the determination of whether information raises an SNQ to only those claims identified by the patent owner in the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the USPTO generally will not review non-identified claims, it is not precluded from doing so. This claim-identification approach may have litigation implications and may be contrary to the plain language of §257(a); courts may ultimately decide scope of unenforceability protection when not all claims are identified.

rubrics_metrics.name: If SNQ found, order ex parte reexamination covering issues in request
rubrics_metrics.description: If the USPTO determines that an SNQ has been raised, it will order ex parte reexamination of the patent directed to all issues (not just prior art issues) addressed in the request that raise an SNQ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ex parte reexamination resulting from supplemental examination will be handled by the Central Reexamination Unit; information first submitted during such reexamination will not be treated as having been considered during supplemental examination for statutory protection purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: No third-party participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Third party participation is prohibited in both the supplemental examination stage and any resulting ex parte reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent owners receive a USPTO-only process; adverse parties cannot participate in the supplemental examination itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory protection against unenforceability (with timing exceptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Following supplemental examination, with certain exceptions, a court may not hold a patent 'unenforceable on the basis of conduct relating to information … that was considered, reconsidered or corrected during a supplemental examination of a patent.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions: (1) if an allegation of unenforceability is particularly pled in a civil action or in an ANDA paragraph iv notice received by the patent owner before the filing date of the supplemental examination request directed to that information, or (2) if an accused infringer raises the defense in an ITC or district court action filed before supplemental examination and any resulting ex parte reexamination are concluded. Thus supplemental exam protection requires appropriate timing relative to litigation or ANDA notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental examination cannot be used to correct material fraud
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplemental examination cannot be used to correct a material fraud that occurred during original prosecution; if the USPTO becomes aware of material fraud during supplemental examination (or resulting reexamination), it will refer the matter to the U.S. Attorney General for appropriate action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A patentee cannot intentionally withhold material information during prosecution and then use supplemental examination to obtain protection just prior to enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Twelve-item limit and counting rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Each supplemental examination is limited to USPTO consideration of no more than twelve items of information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counting rules: (1) a single document submitted counts as one item even if it raises multiple patentability issues (e.g., anticipation and obviousness); (2) multiple documents directed to a single issue count as separate items (e.g., a document and an opponent's email count as two); (3) combinations count separately (a new reference plus two references of record counts as three items); (4) information discussed solely within the request (not contained in a separate document) counts as an item and must be identified by page; (5) a single declaration containing two or more distinct items may be counted as multiple items (subjective determination); (6) items first submitted during any resulting ex parte reexamination will not be considered items 'during supplemental examination' and therefore will not receive supplemental-exam protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types and format of acceptable information; translations
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no limit on the types of information that can be submitted, but all must be written; for non-English-language documents an English-language translation of the necessary and pertinent parts must be submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The USPTO provides little guidance on what qualifies as 'necessary and pertinent' parts; courts are likely not to treat untranslated information as having been addressed in supplemental examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document size fees and redaction policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO charges document size fees for lengthy non-patent documents submitted: $170 for each non-patent document (other than the request) over 20 pages, plus an additional $280 per document for each additional 50 sheets (or fraction thereof) over the first 50 pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Redaction is encouraged to reduce page counts unless redaction removes context; information redacted out of a submitted document will not receive the protection of supplemental examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental examination fees, required payment, and refund rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO will charge $5,140 for conducting supplemental examination and, if ex parte reexamination is ordered as a result, an additional $16,120 for conducting the ex parte reexamination. The patent owner must submit the supplemental examination fee and the ex parte reexamination fee (totaling $21,260) plus any applicable document size fees with the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the USPTO does not order ex parte reexamination, the $16,120 ex parte reexamination fee will be refunded. The supplemental examination fee and document size fees will not be refunded. Supplemental examination fees are not discounted for small and micro entities under the final rule (discounts may be considered in future rulemaking).

rubrics_metrics.name: Content requirements for a request for supplemental examination
rubrics_metrics.description: A request must include: identification of the patent number; a list of the items of information requested to be considered (with page identification and brief description for any item solely contained in the request); a list identifying any other prior or concurrent post-patent USPTO proceedings involving the patent; identification of each claim for which supplemental examination is requested; a separate, detailed explanation of the relevance and manner of applying each item of information to each claim; a copy of the patent and any related certificates; copies of each documentary item (except U.S. patents and patent application publications) with English translations of necessary parts; a summary of relevant portions of any submitted document over 50 pages (with citations); and a showing of ownership establishing the entirety of the ownership interest in the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optional inclusions may include a cover sheet, table of contents, an explanation of how the claims patentably distinguish over items of information, and an explanation of why each item does or does not raise an SNQ. If a request does not comply with all requirements, the USPTO will not grant a filing date until corrected; the filing date will be the date of receipt of the corrected request, not the original.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing-date and correction consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: If a request for supplemental examination does not comply with all requirements, the USPTO will not grant a filing date for the request. A patent owner will be given notice and an opportunity to correct defects, but the filing date is the date of receipt of the corrected request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a defective request is not corrected, supplemental examination will not be conducted and statutory protections will not apply. USPTO will not make a defective request publicly available until accepted for filing date purposes, reducing risk of third-party race to create exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: No amendments or examiner interviews during supplemental examination
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO will not permit amendments (including narrowing claims, cancelling claims, or correcting inventorship) during the supplemental examination stage, even if submitted with the request; examiner interviews are not permitted during supplemental examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments to narrow claims, cancel claims, and to correct inventorship can be made during ex parte reexamination if ordered. Broadening claim amendments are not permitted during supplemental examination or ex parte reexamination. The only opportunity for an examiner interview will be during ex parte reexamination if ordered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim cancellation and disclaimer strategies and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent owner will not be permitted to cancel claims in the request for supplemental examination to avoid reexamination being ordered; however, the owner may choose not to identify such claims in the request or may file a disclaimer of such a claim before requesting supplemental examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A disclaimer is immediately effective upon recordation and can reduce risk of unnecessary reexamination; the USPTO's SNQ determination is limited to claims in effect at the time of determination. The effect of omitting claims from the request on eventual unenforceability protection is uncertain and may be subject to judicial interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counting complexity for declarations and combined items
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO will count a single declaration or affidavit that contains two or more 'distinct' items of information as being two or more items of information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determination of 'distinct' items in a declaration will be subjective in many instances; patent owners should carefully determine item counts on a case-by-case basis to avoid exceeding the twelve-item limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex parte reexamination fee increase for non-supplemental requests
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO increased the fee for all other ex parte reexaminations (i.e., not ordered pursuant to supplemental examination) from $2,520 to $17,750.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the USPTO determines a request for ex parte reexamination does not raise an SNQ, it will refund all but $4,320 of that fee. The ex parte reexamination fee is not reduced for small and micro entities under the final rule; future rulemaking may provide discounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition fee increases
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO will increase most petition fees (including Rule 59, 181, 182, and 183 petitions) in ex parte reexaminations and ongoing inter partes reexaminations from approximately $200–$400 to $1,930.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A few petition fees relating to timing and inventorship correction are exempted from this increase under Rules 550(i) and 937(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex parte reexamination procedural standards and risks
rubrics_metrics.description: Ex parte reexamination is conducted without the presumption of validity and without the clear-and-convincing evidentiary standard applicable in court; patentability is determined under the preponderance-of-the-evidence standard and claims receive their broadest reasonable interpretation consistent with the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reexamination immediately limits enforceability and could result in narrowing or cancellation of claims and creation of estoppels and intervening rights. Reexamination provides limited opportunities for presenting amendments, arguments, and evidence: shortened statutory reply periods (as short as 30 days, up to two months), only one guaranteed opportunity to freely amend rejected claims in response to a first non-final Office Action, extensions not granted as a matter of right, and no RCE or continuing application allowed during ex parte reexamination. A patent owner cannot withdraw from an ex parte reexamination once begun; failure to respond to an Office Action may result in a reexamination certificate adopting positions set forth in the last Office Action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Redress via reissue as an alternative
rubrics_metrics.description: Reissue applications are a potential alternative to supplemental examination to have information considered and can permit amendments, extended response times, RCEs, and further prosecution opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reissue does not provide statutory protection against unenforceability for conduct related to information considered during reissue. Reissue can be lengthy despite special status; Track 1 prioritized examination is not available for reissue. Making a reissue application public may alert infringers and enable preemptive unenforceability allegations before reissue/supplemental examination completes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation: file Information Disclosure Statements during prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent owners should file Information Disclosure Statements (IDS) and otherwise exercise a high level of care to avoid non-disclosure of potentially material information or presentation of erroneous information during initial prosecution, and should not rely on supplemental examination to avoid the cost of doing so during prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplemental examination is expensive and risky and is not a substitute for proper prosecution disclosure practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation: carefully weigh options before requesting supplemental examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent owners should exercise substantial care before deciding to request supplemental examination, including carefully weighing benefits, risks, and costs of alternatives such as disclaimer and/or reissue (optionally followed by supplemental examination) against supplemental examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because of significant fees, potential for material fraud referrals, risk of reexamination, estoppels, and limits on amendments/interviews, consider reissue, disclaimer, timing, and whether supplemental examination will achieve desired protection before litigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation for adverse parties: monitor patents for filings
rubrics_metrics.description: Adverse parties should carefully monitor patents containing claims that may be asserted for indications that a patent owner is considering litigation, including monitoring whether a supplemental examination request has been filed or a reissue application has been filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early detection of filings may inform strategy (e.g., potential to plead unenforceability before supplemental examination concludes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation to expedite ex parte reexamination requests before fee change
rubrics_metrics.description: For anyone considering filing a request for ex parte reexamination, expedite the analysis and, if possible, file before the new (increased) fees come into effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider alternatives (reissue for patent owners; inter partes review and post-grant review for adverse parties) in light of increased fees.
